end.summary:
Practised visualising square and triangular number sequences with dot and coin pictures.
Used rows and columns to represent square numbers, including 5×5, 6×6, 12×12, and 13×13.
Explained that adding one row and one column creates an L-shape, with the corner counted once.
Used 4×4 plus an L-shape of 9 dots to show the growth from 16 to 25.
Teach-back was not completed.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised drawing and reading picture patterns for square and triangular numbers. They used rows, columns, subtraction, and an L-shape to explain how a square grows, including why the corner is counted only once. The main area to revisit is drawing complete dot pictures independently. At home, ask them to sketch 3×3, 4×4, and 5×5 squares and mark the new row, new column, and shared corner.
